title: Late Breaking Results: Novel Design of MTJ-Based Unified LIF Spiking Neuron and PUF
problem: SNNs offer superior energy and hardware efficiency over DNNs but lack effective security mechanisms; integrating security with neuromorphic computing requires both functional neuromorphic circuits and cryptographic key generation.
motivation: SNNs process sensitive data requiring protection; physically unclonable functions (PUFs) enable device authentication and cryptographic key generation, making MTJ-based unified neuron/PUF designs valuable for secure neuromorphic systems.
method: Proposes an MTJ-based LIF (Leaky Integrate-and-Fire) neuron that simultaneously functions as both a spiking neuron and physically unclonable function (PUF). The design leverages MTJ's magnetic properties for dual-mode operation through unified circuit architecture.
key_novelty: First unified MTJ-based circuit functioning as both LIF spiking neuron and PUF, combining neuromorphic computing with hardware-based security through single integrated device.
contributions: Mean Shannon entropy of 0.9974 for 128-bit PUF response (near ideal 1.0)
Enables secure neuromorphic systems with integrated authentication and cryptography
baselines: conventional separate neuron and PUF designs
limitations: Monte Carlo simulation results only; silicon implementation and reliability under noise/temperature variation not evaluated.
primary_theme: Integrated MTJ-based spiking neuron with embedded PUF for secure neuromorphic computing
